newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria, Russia, Greece study Balkans oil pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria, Russia, Greece study Balkans oil pipeline.

text.p: Bulgarian, Russian and Greek experts have agreed to set up a consortium to assign projects for a planned oil route supplying Russian crude to the Balkans, Bulgaria's public works ministry said on Monday.

A ministry statement said a tripartite meeting of experts had discussed in Sofia over the weekend the preparation of tender documents for the construction of an oil pipeline from Bourgas in Bulgaria to Alexandroupolis in Greece, bypassing the Bosphorous.

"Experts from the three countries have agreed to establish a tripartite engineering consortium which will assign the preparation of the projects and monitor their performance," a ministry statement said.
Russia, Bulgaria and Greece plan a tanker route from the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiisk to Bourgas from where the new pipeline would carry Russian crude to Alexandroupolis.

The meeting also discussed the type of equipment to be installed next to Bourgas and Alexandroupolis, the statement said. The next meeting will be held at the end of August or the beginning of September. -- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
